short: A narrow Swedish victory bought at the price of the king who won it.
full:
Wallenstein had been recalled to command the imperial army and had drawn up along the Leipzig road near Lützen, roadside ditches deepened into a trench line across his front, when Gustavus Adolphus attacked on 16 November 1632. Fog held the Swedish start until eleven in the morning and confused the fighting for the rest of the day.

Gustavus rode with the cavalry on his right, became separated from his escort in the smoke, and was shot several times; his horse came back without him. Bernard of Saxe-Weimar took command, pressed the attack, and held the field when Wallenstein withdrew overnight leaving his artillery behind. Sweden had the victory and had lost the man who directed its policy. Chancellor Axel Oxenstierna took over the war and the German alliances, but no successor could hold the Protestant coalition together in the same way. The date given is Gregorian; Swedish accounts of the time, on the Julian calendar, date the battle 6 November.
